slug: 残简道藏我靠修复古籍证道
content_zh:
玄洲界，青云仙宗，西藏书阁。
昏沉天光顺着朽木窗棂的缝隙斜切进来，浮尘在光柱里缓缓翻涌，落满层层叠叠的竹简与帛书。空气里弥漫着陈旧木简、霉纸与淡淡墨香混杂的味道，沉闷压抑，一如沈砚在此度过的三年岁月。
他垂着眉眼，指尖抚过一卷边缘腐朽、大半字迹模糊的竹册，指腹那层常年翻书磨出的薄茧蹭过干裂竹纹，触感粗糙刺人。身上那件洗得发白的灰布杂役长袍松松垮垮罩在清瘦挺拔的身躯上，木簪简单束起长发，发间还沾着少许书卷灰尘，任谁初见，都只会当他是个无足轻重的底层杂役。
可三年前，他不是这般模样。
彼时沈砚乃是青云仙宗外门最具潜力的文道修士，十五岁凝出道基，通读百卷正统道书，宗门长老皆断言，不出五年，他便能叩开内门大门，踏上更高文道。
奈何人心叵测，同门陆明远觊觎他偶然所得的半卷上古道册，暗中设下圈套栽赃他偷盗宗门至宝，又买通执掌刑罚的周长老，借审讯之机，以文道碎印重创他先天道基。
道基崩裂，灵气溃散，一身修为十不存一。昔日天才一夜沦为废人，宗门不愿斩杀曾经看好的弟子，便将他发配至最为偏僻荒凉的西藏书阁，名为看管古籍，实则形同流放。
三年光阴，春去秋来。
阁内管事克扣他每月微薄的灵石供给，外门弟子途经藏书阁，时常进来肆意嘲讽，拿他这个跌落尘埃的昔日天才取乐。沈砚性子藏着文人傲骨，却深知自身道基破损，无力抗衡，只得收敛所有锋芒，默默清扫书卷、整理残简，将所有委屈与不甘尽数压在心底。
“沈砚，速速出来！”
一道张扬跋扈的少年声响自藏书阁门外炸开，脚步声踏得木质台阶咚咚作响，带着毫不掩饰的轻蔑。
沈砚指尖一顿，缓缓抬眼，眼底掠过一丝极淡的冷意，转瞬又归于平静，低头将手中残简轻轻放在木架之上，转身朝着阁门走去。
门外站着的正是陆明远，一身崭新月白内门弟子长袍，腰间悬挂储物玉袋，灵气萦绕周身，早已是今非昔比。他身后跟着两名跟班外门弟子，皆是一脸戏谑，目光肆无忌惮地扫过沈砚身上破旧的灰布长袍。
“三年不见，沈大天才倒是越发落魄了，整日与一堆破烂竹简为伴，滋味如何？”陆明远双手背在身后，缓步踏入藏书阁，目光扫过四周堆积如山的朽坏古籍，唇角勾起一抹讥讽的弧度，“也是，道基碎了，再也参悟不了正统道文，也就只配守着这些没人看得上的残卷苟活。”
身旁跟班顺势附和：“陆师兄如今已是内门核心弟子，哪里还记得当年和废人一同修行的日子。”
“听说这西阁的旧简全是要丢弃的废料，沈砚天天整理，莫不是想从破烂里找出什么机缘？真是痴心妄想。”
刺耳的话语钻入耳中，沈砚脊背依旧挺直，没有半分佝偻，平静望向陆明远：“阁下无事，便请离开，此处乃是藏书重地，不容喧哗。”
他声音清淡，不卑不亢，没有半分乞怜，也未曾动怒嘶吼。
这份淡然落在陆明远眼中，反倒更令他心生不快。当年他费尽心思毁掉沈砚道基，就是想看对方跪地求饶、一蹶不振的模样，可三年过去，这人依旧一副波澜不惊的姿态，仿佛从未将他的算计放在眼里。
“藏书重地？一堆朽烂废纸也配称重地？”陆明远冷笑一声，随手伸手一把扫过身侧木架，数卷残破竹简哗啦啦摔落在地，竹片断裂，尘封的灰尘漫天扬起。

其中一卷最为老旧的黑纹竹简直直滚到沈砚脚边，简身裂痕遍布，大半篆刻古字都被霉斑覆盖，看起来毫无价值。
“我今日便毁了这些破烂，看你能奈我何。”陆明远居高临下地俯视沈砚，眼底满是得意，“你的道基早已破碎，一身灵气近乎断绝，就算心中怨恨，又能拿我怎样？”
两名跟班站在一旁哄笑，等着看沈砚气急败坏却无力反抗的狼狈模样。
沈砚垂眸看向脚边那卷破损竹简，目光骤然一凝。
心底压抑三年的委屈、不甘、怒火在此刻隐隐翻涌，他攥紧手掌，指节泛白。他清楚自己如今修为低微，硬碰硬只会招来更严苛的责罚，可看着承载文道传承的古简被肆意损毁，文人骨子里的惜道之心难以按捺。
他弯腰，想要拾起地上散落的竹简。
content_en:
Xuanzhou Realm, Qingyun Immortal Sect, Tibet Book Pavilion.
The dim skylight came in diagonally along the cracks in the rotten wooden window lattice, and floating dust slowly surged in the light beam, covering the layers of bamboo slips and silk books. The air is filled with the mixed smell of old wooden slips, moldy paper and the faint scent of ink. It is dull and depressing, just like the three years Shen Yan spent here.
He lowered his eyebrows and stroked his fingertips over a bamboo volume with rotten edges and half of the handwriting blurred. The thin layer of calluses on his fingertips rubbed against the dry cracked bamboo texture, making it rough and stinging to the touch. The washed-white gray cloth handyman robe on his body was loose and covered his thin and tall body. His long hair was simply tied up with a wooden hairpin, and there was still a little book dust in his hair. Anyone who saw him for the first time would just think that he was an insignificant low-level handyman.
But three years ago, he was not like this.
At that time, Shen Yan was the most promising literary monk in the outer sect of Qingyun Immortal Sect. He had established his Taoist foundation at the age of fifteen and read hundreds of orthodox Taoist books. The elders of the sect all asserted that within five years, he would be able to knock on the door of the inner sect and embark on a higher literary path.
Unexpectedly, Lu Mingyuan, a fellow sect member, coveted the half-volume ancient Taoist book he had obtained by chance, and secretly set a trap to frame him for stealing the sect's treasure. He also bribed Elder Zhou, who was in charge of punishments, and used the opportunity of interrogation to severely damage his innate Taoist foundation with the broken seal of Wen Tao.
The foundation of the Tao collapsed, the spiritual energy collapsed, and there was no trace of his cultivation. The former genius turned into a useless person overnight. The sect did not want to kill the once promising disciple, so he was sent to the most remote and desolate Tibetan library. The name was to guard ancient books, but in fact it was the same as exile.
In three years, spring passed and autumn came.
The stewards in the pavilion deducted his meager monthly supply of spiritual stones. The outer disciples passing by the library often came in to ridicule him and make fun of him, a former genius who had fallen into the dust. Shen Yan's temperament hides the arrogance of a scholar, but he knows that his moral foundation is damaged and he is unable to compete, so he has to restrain all his sharp edges, silently clean the books, sort out the fragments, and suppress all the grievances and unwillingness in his heart.
"Shen Yan, come out quickly!"
An arrogant and domineering young man's voice exploded from outside the library door, and the footsteps made the wooden steps clang, with undisguised contempt.
Shen Yan paused with his fingertips and slowly raised his eyes. A faint coldness flashed across his eyes. In an instant, he calmed down again. He lowered his head and gently placed the broken slip in his hand on the wooden frame, then turned and walked towards the door of the pavilion.
Standing outside the door was none other than Lu Mingyuan, dressed in a brand-new moon-white inner sect disciple's robe, with a storage jade bag hanging around his waist. His spiritual energy was lingering around him. He was no longer what he used to be. Behind him were two followers from the outer sect, both of whom had joking expressions on their faces, and their eyes unscrupulously swept over Shen Yan's worn gray cloth robe.
"We haven't seen each other for three years. Shen Dacai has become more and more depressed. How does it feel to be with a pile of tattered bamboo slips all day long?" Lu Mingyuan put his hands behind his back and slowly stepped into the library. His eyes glanced at the piles of decayed ancient books around him, and the corner of his lips curled up with a sarcastic arc. "That's right, the Taoist foundation is broken. He can no longer understand the orthodox Taoist scriptures, so he can only live with these fragments that no one values."
The follower beside him echoed: "Senior Brother Lu is now a core disciple of the inner sect. How can he still remember the days when he practiced with the useless people?"
"I heard that the old slips in the West Pavilion are all scraps that need to be discarded. Shen Yan sorts them out every day. Could it be that he wants to find some opportunity in the tatters? What a wishful thinking."
The harsh words penetrated into his ears. Shen Yan's back was still straight, without any rickets. He looked at Lu Mingyuan calmly: "If you have nothing to do, please leave. This is a place where books are collected, and no noise is allowed."
His voice was light, neither humble nor arrogant, neither begging for mercy nor roaring in anger.
This indifference fell into Lu Mingyuan's eyes, which made him even more unhappy. Back then, he tried his best to destroy Shen Yan Daoji, just to see him kneel down and beg for mercy, helpless. But three years later, this man still looked calm, as if he had never paid attention to his plans.
"A great collection of books? A pile of decayDoes waste paper also deserve a weighing site? "Lu Mingyuan sneered, then reached out and swept the wooden frame beside him. Several rolls of broken bamboo slips fell to the ground with a crash. The bamboo pieces broke and dust filled the sky.
One of the oldest rolls of black-patterned bamboo rolled almost to Shen Yan's feet. It was covered with cracks and most of the ancient seal characters were covered with mildew, making it look worthless.
"I will destroy these rags today to see what you can do to me. "Lu Mingyuan looked down at Shen Yan, his eyes full of pride, "Your Taoist foundation has long been broken, and your spiritual energy is almost cut off. Even if you are resentful in your heart, what can you do to me? "
The two followers stood aside and laughed, waiting to see Shen Yan's embarrassment, furious but unable to resist.
Shen Yan lowered his eyes and looked at the damaged bamboo slips at his feet, and his eyes suddenly focused.
The grievances, unwillingness, and anger that had been suppressed for three years in his heart were faintly rising at this moment. He clenched his palms tightly, and his knuckles turned white. He knew that his cultivation level was low now, and a head-on confrontation would only lead to harsher punishments. However, seeing the ancient slips that carried the inheritance of literature and ethics being wantonly destroyed, the literati's cherishing of ethics in their bones was hard to suppress.
He bent down and wanted to pick up the bamboo slips scattered on the ground.
